bug_semantics: Ech0 treated access-token scopes as an opt-in route property rather than an invariant of authenticated access. A deliberately low-scope token for an administrator (for example, echo:read) was accepted by the shared JWT middleware on privileged routes that omitted RequireScopes; downstream services commonly checked only the account's IsAdmin bit. The public backup export path was worse: it reparsed a query token and rebuilt viewer state from only claims.Userid, dropping token type, scopes, audience, and JTI, so the same low-scope token could export the database ZIP.
flaw_origin: The smallest reconstructed origin is PR #195 member bf994ebfd5fe2e16b85ff64ad25147abd9ba99d7. It first changed AccessTokenSettingDto and CreateAccessToken to accept, validate, persist, and sign caller-selected Scopes and Audience, thereby creating tokens represented as least-privileged while the existing authenticated and backup routes still authorized without those scopes. Its immediate parent 387667192911c86db1e1bcb3f544ce12d340ffdb minted only unscoped access tokens, so the scoped least-privilege contract that could be bypassed did not yet exist. Later member b47fa1c75d890cd080e3f6699bbfca8cd8d4b939 added RequireScopes only to selected echo/file/setting/user routes, leaving inbox, panel comments, connects, migration, dashboard, and backup outside the guard; squash commit 3f8fb150158723aca31df2ae937a1aa7b31ac254 landed the completed PR.

evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/security/advisories/GHSA-4h9q-p5j4-xvvh describes affected versions <=4.3.4, patched version 4.4.3, successful /api/inbox access with an echo:read-only admin token, and /api/backup/export returning a ZIP containing ech0.db and app.log. It identifies opt-in RequireScopes, admin-only service checks, and backup viewer reconstruction as the causal authorization split.

The GitHub PR #195 commit endpoint https://api.github.com/repos/lin-snow/Ech0/pulls/195/commits reconstructs the squash members. Member bf994ebfd5fe2e16b85ff64ad25147abd9ba99d7 has parent 387667192911c86db1e1bcb3f544ce12d340ffdb and message 'feat(setting): add scoped access token schema and validation' with exact commit-message marker 'Made-with: Cursor'. Its patch adds Scopes and Audience to internal/model/setting/setting_dto.go and changes internal/service/setting/access_token_service.go to normalize scopes and call CreateAccessClaimsWithExpiry(user, expiry, scopes, audience, jti).

Direct parent-tree verification used https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lin-snow/Ech0/387667192911c86db1e1bcb3f544ce12d340ffdb/internal/service/setting/access_token_service.go: the parent reads only Name and Expiry and calls CreateClaimsWithExpiry(user, expiry), with no scopes or audience. The BIC tree at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lin-snow/Ech0/bf994ebfd5fe2e16b85ff64ad25147abd9ba99d7/internal/service/setting/access_token_service.go contains the new scope/audience validation, signing, and persistence. Thus the low-scope token contract is absent in the immediate parent and present in the BIC.

PR member b47fa1c75d890cd080e3f6699bbfca8cd8d4b939 (https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/commit/b47fa1c75d890cd080e3f6699bbfca8cd8d4b939) creates internal/middleware/scope.go and adds guards only in internal/router/{echo,file,setting,user}.go. Its seven-file diff does not touch internal/router/inbox.go, comment.go, connect.go, migration.go, dashboard.go, or common.go, confirming that the merged enforcement design remained opt-in and incomplete.

reasoning: The privileged routes and backup's identity-only viewer reconstruction predated scoped tokens, so those older commits alone did not violate a scope contract. PR #195 introduced the contract in a squash. Decomposing its public member chain isolates bf994ebfd5fe2e16b85ff64ad25147abd9ba99d7 as the first commit that let an administrator mint a JWT explicitly limited by scopes and audience. The direct parent did not accept or encode those restrictions, satisfying immediate-parent absence. Subsequent members propagated metadata and added an opt-in RequireScopes middleware to only a subset of routes; they did not remove the already-present bypass and instead left the advisory's privileged surfaces uncovered. Squash 3f8fb150158723aca31df2ae937a1aa7b31ac254 put that member tree on main before v4.2.1 and it remained in v4.3.4. Direct fix 6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313 both covers the omitted routes and preserves the authenticated viewer context for backup, and its first containing release is v4.4.3. AI judgment is restricted to the decomposed BIC object: human authorship plus exact 'Made-with: Cursor' is explicit AI assistance tied to the code-bearing origin, but is weaker than bot authorship or an AI Co-Authored-By identity; therefore AI_CODE_FLAWED is more precise than AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
